blocks.text: Genesis 34 begins with Dinah going out to see the daughters of the land and Shechem taking her and lying with her. Hamor and Shechem seek marriage, while Jacob's sons answer with guile by requiring circumcision of the city's males. On the third day, when the men are sore, Simeon and Levi kill the males, retrieve Dinah, and the other sons plunder the city and take its people and goods. Jacob fears the consequences among the surrounding inhabitants, while his sons answer by appealing to what was done to their sister.

The chapter gives no simple narrator's endorsement of the actions that follow Dinah's violation. It records Shechem's desire, the brothers' deception, the slaughter, the plunder, Jacob's fear, and the brothers' final question. Commentary should preserve those tensions and distinguish the canonical account of what the characters did from an unsupported claim that the text resolves every moral or cultural question surrounding their actions.
